walkthroughs.body_html:
Statistical Distributions — a core area of A-Level Maths.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Statistical Distributions brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Statistical Distributions.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Can a probability ever be greater than 1?
options: The area of a circle is pi * d, where d is the diameter.
Yes — if an event is very likely, the probability can be 1.5 or 2.
Yes, but only when expressed as a percentage.
No — probabilities range from 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain).

mcqs.q: What does the number pi (~ 3.14159...) actually represent?
options: Pi is a fixed length, like the radius of a special unit circle.
The ratio of any circle's circumference to its diameter — a constant that is the same for all circles.
Pi is just a label for a difficult number with no specific meaning.
The area of a circle is pi * d, where d is the diameter.

mcqs.q: What is the formula for the area of a circle?
options: The area of a circle is pi * d, where d is the diameter.
pi * r^2 (pi times the radius squared).
The area of a circle is 2 * pi * r — the same as the circumference formula.
Pi is just a label for a difficult number with no specific meaning.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Probability mass function”?
options: E(X) = Σx·p(x) (discrete) or ∫x·f(x) dx (continuous). Long-run average value.
PMF p(x) gives P(X = x) for discrete X. Σp(x) = 1. Used to define distribution.
Var(X) = E(X²) − [E(X)]². Spread of distribution. SD = √Var(X).
PDF f(x) for continuous X. P(a ≤ X ≤ b) = ∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx. Total area under curve = 1.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Variance”?
options: PDF f(x) for continuous X. P(a ≤ X ≤ b) = ∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx. Total area under curve = 1.
PMF p(x) gives P(X = x) for discrete X. Σp(x) = 1. Used to define distribution.
E(aX + b) = aE(X) + b; Var(aX + b) = a²Var(X). For independent X, Y: Var(X+Y) = Var(X) + Var(Y).
Var(X) = E(X²) − [E(X)]². Spread of distribution. SD = √Var(X).

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Expectation”?
options: Var(X) = E(X²) − [E(X)]². Spread of distribution. SD = √Var(X).
E(X) = Σx·p(x) (discrete) or ∫x·f(x) dx (continuous). Long-run average value.
PDF f(x) for continuous X. P(a ≤ X ≤ b) = ∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx. Total area under curve = 1.
E(aX + b) = aE(X) + b; Var(aX + b) = a²Var(X). For independent X, Y: Var(X+Y) = Var(X) + Var(Y).

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Probability density function”?
options: E(X) = Σx·p(x) (discrete) or ∫x·f(x) dx (continuous). Long-run average value.
PDF f(x) for continuous X. P(a ≤ X ≤ b) = ∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx. Total area under curve = 1.
E(aX + b) = aE(X) + b; Var(aX + b) = a²Var(X). For independent X, Y: Var(X+Y) = Var(X) + Var(Y).
Var(X) = E(X²) − [E(X)]². Spread of distribution. SD = √Var(X).

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Linear combinations”?
options: E(aX + b) = aE(X) + b; Var(aX + b) = a²Var(X). For independent X, Y: Var(X+Y) = Var(X) + Var(Y).
E(X) = Σx·p(x) (discrete) or ∫x·f(x) dx (continuous). Long-run average value.
PDF f(x) for continuous X. P(a ≤ X ≤ b) = ∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx. Total area under curve = 1.
Discrete: countable outcomes (binomial, Poisson). Continuous: any value in an interval (normal, exponential).

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Discrete vs continuous”?
options: Var(X) = E(X²) − [E(X)]². Spread of distribution. SD = √Var(X).
PDF f(x) for continuous X. P(a ≤ X ≤ b) = ∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx. Total area under curve = 1.
E(X) = Σx·p(x) (discrete) or ∫x·f(x) dx (continuous). Long-run average value.
Discrete: countable outcomes (binomial, Poisson). Continuous: any value in an interval (normal, exponential).
